module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 729

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/729](https://www.erdosproblems.com/729)
- [EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., *On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$*. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.
- [Er68c] Erdős, P., *Aufgabe 557*. Elemente Math. (1968), 111-113.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos729

/--
Let $C>0$ be a constant. Are there infinitely many integers $a,b,n$ with $a+b> n+C\log n$ such
that the denominator of $$\frac{n!}{a!b!}$$contains only primes $\ll_C 1$?

Erdős [Er68c] proved that if $a!b!\mid n!$ then $a+b\leq n+O(\log n)$. This has been proved in the affirmative by Barreto and Leeham, using ChatGPT and Aristotle, with a modification of the argument used for [728].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos729.lean"]
theorem erdos_729 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ (C : ℝ) (hC : C > 0),
      ∃ K ≥ 3, Set.Infinite { T : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ |
        let (a, b, n) := T
        a > 0 ∧ b > 0 ∧ n > 0 ∧
        (a : ℝ) + b > n + C * Real.log n ∧
        ∀ p, p.Prime → p > K →
          padicValNat p ((n.factorial / (a.factorial * b.factorial) : ℚ).den) = 0 } := by
  sorry

end Erdos729

reformulations.difference: EGRS75, p. 91, asks for infinitely many n admitting suitable a,b and a uniform bound on denominator prime divisors. Lean instead requires infinitely many triples (a,b,n), expresses the prime restriction using zero p-adic valuations, and requires the existential cutoff K to be at least 3.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a prime p and a rational's nonzero reduced denominator d, padicValNat p d = 0 iff p does not divide d. For fixed n and K, choose a prime q > max(n,K). Since q does not divide n!, the denominator condition forces a < q and b < q; otherwise q survives in the reduced denominator. Thus each n-fiber contains finitely many admissible triples, so infinitely many triples is equivalent to infinitely many admissible n. Finally, replacing any cutoff K by max(K,3) preserves admissibility. The combined pointwise equivalence was proved as Review729.full_formulation_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, independently of the problem's sorry.

review.notes: The sole declaration is faithful. Elaboration and small computations confirm rational division before taking the reduced denominator; the valuation's exceptional zero cases cannot affect the prime condition. The cited external proof has exactly the required conclusion and contains no sorry or custom axioms; the public status database records 729 as proved (Lean), matching answer(True) and research solved. The upstream proof was inspected, not rebuilt under its older toolchain. Direct requests to erdosproblems.com/729 and its forum returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so the statement was checked against the cited primary literature and the status corroborated separately. Scratch checks compile successfully; the equivalence proofs depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
